GenerateMoveStateMachine.maps_to: the __init__ slot branch and stunned flag (phrog_parasite.py:33-35) + the take_turn alternation (phrog_parasite.py:49-60)
GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: CORRECTION to SHARED-FINDINGS section 0, same as nibbit: Wriggler.cs:57 builds a ConditionalBranchState, not a RandomBranchState, so it draws nothing (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54) and no distribution argument is owed. Graph: SPAWNED_MOVE (a no-op with StunIntent, Wriggler.cs:73-76) -> INIT_MOVE; INIT_MOVE picks NASTY_BITE for SlotName wriggler1/wriggler3 and WRIGGLE for wriggler2/wriggler4 (:58-61); then NASTY_BITE <-> WRIGGLE forever (:63-64). Initial state is SPAWNED_MOVE if StartStunned else INIT_MOVE (:69). The port maps the slot rule to `slot % 2 == 1` and resolves it in the constructor. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain`, slots 1-4, 20 turns): sequences identical and 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides for every slot.

guards.what: The StartStunned arm: C# performs a real SPAWNED_MOVE node for one turn; the sim sets `self.stunned = start_stunned` (phrog_parasite.py:33) and lets the combat loop skip the turn
guards.rationale: Same observable, established by reading both loops rather than assumed. C#: the machine's initial state is SPAWNED_MOVE, a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky rule makes the AfterCreatureAdded roll a no-op with no draw; the creature telegraphs StunIntent, performs `return Task.CompletedTask`, and the NEXT roll walks SPAWNED_MOVE -> INIT_MOVE -> the slot move. Sim: `combat.py:313-329` skips take_turn and clears the flag, current_intent returns Intent(MoveType.STUN) (phrog_parasite.py:39-40), and _move_key already holds the slot move. Both give: turn 1 a stun intent and no action, turn 2 the slot move, zero MonsterAi draws throughout. Note this is NOT monster_state_machine G4/G5's subject -- no CreatureCmd.stun is involved on either side, the deferral is the graph's own SPAWNED_MOVE node, and Wriggler has no RandomBranchState whose weights a log entry could move.

guards.what: INTRA-MOVE ORDER INVERSION in WRIGGLE: C# adds the Infection card FIRST and applies StrengthPower 2 SECOND (Wriggler.cs:99-100); the port applies Strength first and adds the card second (phrog_parasite.py:56-59)
guards.rationale: The only intra-move order inversion in this batch, so it was executed rather than eyeballed. `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py order` runs one WRIGGLE turn twice from the same seed -- shipped order and the C# order -- and diffs 12 observable keys (player HP, block and powers; all four card piles by id and position; the monster's HP, block and powers; the MonsterAi and Shuffle stream counters): differences NONE. The two effects touch disjoint state and neither dispatch reads the other's: add_to_discard appends and fires on_card_entered_combat (cmds.py:464-472), whose ported listeners afflict the card, while PowerCmd.apply fires modify_power_amount / on_power_applied, whose ported listeners (relics/ruined_helmet.py, relics/unsettling_lamp.py) gate on the player. BOUND OF THE EVIDENCE, stated per rule 5: the probe runs with no relics and no player powers, so it proves independence of the two commands, not of every possible future listener. Concrete trigger that would make the order matter: any on_card_entered_combat listener that reads the applier's Strength, or any modify_power_amount listener that reads a pile count.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 5-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 21 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [17,21], observed [17,21], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 21 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
